hints.title: Inverting Left Backbone Links
hints.text: Turn the leftmost node into the new root, making its sibling the left child and its parent the right child.

hints.title: Iterative Pointer Relinking
hints.text: Walk along the left spine keeping track of previous parent and previous right sibling, rotating connections step by step.

hints.title: In-Place Tree Inversion
hints.text: Initialize curr = root, prev = null, prev_right = null. While curr is not null, save curr.left and curr.right. Set curr.left = prev_right and curr.right = prev. Update prev = curr, prev_right = next_right, and curr = next_left. Return prev.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
from typing import Optional

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right

class Solution:
    def upsideDownBinaryTree(self, root: Optional[TreeNode]) -> Optional[TreeNode]:
        curr = root
        prev = None
        prev_right = None
        while curr:
            next_left = curr.left
            next_right = curr.right
            curr.left = prev_right
            curr.right = prev
            prev = curr
            prev_right = next_right
            curr = next_left
        return prev
```

variables: H: height of binary tree (length of left spine)
complexity.notes: Optimal iterative in-place pointer reversal in O(H) time and O(1) space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Deep recursive solutions consume O(H) call stack frames.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Iterative 3-pointer swapping executes in constant auxiliary memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Rotate the left spine so curr.left becomes right sibling and curr.right becomes parent.
